name: Genuine False Flag — Real Attack with Contradictory Attribution
description: A real compromise: process hollowing and LSASS credential dumping confirmed in memory (hard-to-fake structural evidence). On top of the real attack, the operator planted suspiciously pristine Russian-language strings whose profile contradicts the actual TTPs and OPSEC. This is what a real false flag looks like: the malicious event is PRESENT, and the attribution is engineered to misdirect. MALICE is correct here — and it belongs to the framer, not to any Russian-speaker.
audit_note: Finding H-02. Positive counterpart of FP-CULTURAL-CLEAN-001. With the current rule (which requires LOW technical for FALSE_FLAG_PATTERN) this genuine false flag is NOT detected. After the fix, detection must be based on attribution/technical-profile mismatch, not on the absence of technical evidence.

artifacts.description: Process hollowing in svchost.exe confirmed (T1055.012). Reflective DLL injection. Structural, hard-to-fake evidence of a real intrusion.
LSASS credential dumping detected (T1003.001). Active compromise, not a clean system.
Suspiciously pristine Russian-language strings injected into the dropper, inconsistent with the actor's actual toolchain and OPSEC. Attribution markers contradict the observed technical TTP profile.

caie_fractures.interpretation: A real intrusion is present, but the attribution markers are too clean and contradict the actor's actual TTP profile. The malice is the deliberate misdirection. Proposed rule: false flag requires a corroborated malicious event AND attribution inconsistent with it — not the mere absence of technical evidence.

peirce_chain.firstness: Russian strings present alongside confirmed injection and credential dumping.
peirce_chain.secondness: The attribution profile contradicts the technical TTPs; the markers are too clean for the OPSEC observed.
peirce_chain.thirdness: The real attacker staged the attribution to misdirect blame. The deception is the malicious act.

demo_quote: The real false flag has the attack present. The malice belongs to the planter, not to the language of the flag.
